question: Which cells in the body are responsible for producing antibodies?
explanation: Plasma cells develop from activated B lymphocytes and specialize in making and releasing antibodies into body fluids. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h1)

question: Why does a newborn baby depend heavily on antibodies from the mother right after birth?

options.A: The newborn liver fails to produce adequate blood proteins.
options.B: The placenta blocks all blood cells permanently.
options.C: Breast milk destroys all internal infant bacteria.
options.D: The baby's immune system is still immature and has not met many germs yet.

explanation: A baby is born with an inexperienced immune system that needs maternal antibodies for early protection against environmental germs. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h1)

question: What shape is used to describe the basic structure of an antibody molecule?
explanation: Antibodies are built like the letter Y, with branching arms for binding and a straight stem. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h2)

question: What is the main job of the tips located at the top of an antibody?

options.A: Attaching directly to specific foreign germs
options.B: Producing new red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: Filtering waste products out of the lymphatic fluid
options.D: Releasing stored chemical energy into the blood

explanation: The tips of the Y-shaped antibody are designed to lock precisely onto matching antigens found on invading germs. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h2)

question: Which antibody is the first responder found circulating in the blood during a new, recent infection?
explanation: IgM is the largest antibody and forms the first line of defense when the body encounters a brand-new germ for the first time. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h3)

question: A patient has severe itching and swelling from a food allergy, involving antibodies bound to mast cells. Which antibody class is involved?
explanation: IgE antibodies attach to mast cells and trigger the release of histamines, causing allergic symptoms. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h3)

question: Which antibody type is found in the highest amount in normal human blood?
explanation: IgG makes up the majority of circulating antibodies in the blood and provides long-lasting protection. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h4)

question: Why is the structure of IgM effective at clumping foreign cells together?

options.A: It dissolves completely into fatty tissue layers for storage.
options.B: It links five antibody units together into a star-like shape.
options.C: It changes its chemical color when touching bacteria.
options.D: It is small enough to slip through tiny capillary walls easily.

explanation: Because IgM links five units together, it has ten binding sites to grab multiple germs at once and form clumps. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h4)

question: Which antibody can cross the placenta to reach the developing fetus?
explanation: Special receptors on the placenta transport maternal IgG into fetal circulation to provide passive immunity before birth. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h5)

question: Why are babies born prematurely at a higher risk of getting early infections?

options.A: They miss the heavy third-trimester transfer of maternal IgG from the placenta.
options.B: Their bodies immediately destroy all forms of secretory IgA.
options.C: The umbilical cord retains bacteria directly from the placenta.
options.D: Breast milk completely lacks any protective immune proteins.

explanation: Most maternal IgG crosses the placenta during the final weeks of pregnancy, so preterm babies miss out on this transfer. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of giving Anti-D immunoglobulin to a Rhesus-negative pregnant woman?

options.A: To stimulate the immediate production of maternal breast milk
options.B: To lower high maternal blood pressure during the third trimester
options.C: To prevent her immune system from forming antibodies against fetal red blood cells
options.D: To cure existing bacterial infections within the amniotic fluid cavity

explanation: Anti-D immunoglobulin clears any fetal Rhesus-positive cells that enter the mother's circulation before her immune system reacts to them. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h6)

question: Why are routine infant immunizations spread out over several months instead of giving them all at birth?

options.A: Vaccine medications spoil easily inside a young infant's stomach.
options.B: Infant skin is too fragile to tolerate more than one needle puncture.
options.C: Newborn kidneys instantly filter out all injected liquid medicines.
options.D: Remaining maternal antibodies can destroy vaccine components if given too early.

explanation: High levels of maternal IgG passed from the mother can neutralize vaccine antigens before the baby's own immune system can learn from them. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h6)
